title: Delegated enclave collector routing for tenant-bounded observability in Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Dedicated and Private deployments need stronger tenant isolation for telemetry without forcing per-tenant collectors per host. Goal: implement a Delegated Enclave Collector Routing pattern: a small, per-host secure enclave process accepts signed telemetry envelopes, performs tenant-aware routing and admission checks, and forwards to tenant-scoped pipelines (either shared cluster namespaces or tenant-specific relays) while preserving trace continuity and minimizing latency. This ticket designs and implements the routing shim, admission policy hooks for RBAC/quotas, and the tracing hook adapter to preserve span IDs and parent links across routing hops. Scope excludes long-term storage retention policy changes and UI work beyond adding collector health tiles in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Enclave routing shim deployed to Dedicated and Private test clusters that can accept signed envelopes and route to tenant pipelines using tenant-id headers
Tracing hooks maintain trace-id and parent-span across routing (end-to-end traces from edge -> enclave -> ingress pipeline) verified by synthetic workloads
Per-tenant admission checks enforce soft and hard quotas; violations are emitted as structured logs and metrics
Latency overhead introduced by enclave routing < 5ms p50 for telemetry handoff under normal load
Automated integration tests that simulate tenant traffic spikes and validate no cross-tenant leakage
Canary rollout plan documented and rollback hooks implemented
Design and implementation reviewed and approved by Security and Platform Reliability

progress_updates: 2026-02-14: Kickoff meeting with Platform, Security, and SRE. Agreed on envelope signing using tenant-specific HMAC keys managed via customer KMS for Private deployments.
2026-02-20: Prototype of routing shim accepts signed envelopes and routes to namespace-based sinks. Early perf shows ~3.2ms additional latency on p50 in dev cluster.
2026-02-28: Tracing adapter implemented for HTTP/gRPC. Verified trace continuity across shim with local end-to-end synthetic traces. Need to validate with real sampling rates.
2026-03-04: Security review flagged key rotation edge-case for long-lived collector sessions; added short token TTL and token refresh handshake to design.
2026-03-08: Integration test harness created. Began simulated spike test to verify admission behavior; observed soft-quota backpressure works but requires tuning of sampling thresholds.
2026-03-10: Internal RFC posted with design diagrams and rollout plan. Requesting PM sign-off and SRE canary window scheduling.
review_feedback: PM (Harper Lee): Ensure canary includes both Dedicated and Private flavors; list acceptance criteria differences for on-prem (no central KMS).
Security (Diego Morales): Prefer envelope signing with per-collector ephemeral keys and KMS-backed delegation for Private. Confirmed threat model ok pending rotation story.
SRE (Lin Zhao): Add health signal for pending queue length and last-successful-forward timestamp. Require alert thresholds before canary promotion.
Design (Marta Silva): Console tile should visualize per-tenant ingress rate, rejected/soft-failed envelopes, and representative p95 latency.
risks: Key rotation failure could orphan long-lived collectors in Private air-gapped installs
Misconfiguration of tenant routing could cause elevated cross-tenant tails if admission policies fail
Performance degradation if enclave process is co-located on already-saturated hosts
Operator complexity increase for customers who expect single binary collectors
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal dev cluster testing + synthetic workloads (2 weeks). Phase 2: Canary in Dedicated non-production pools with 5% traffic and SRE monitoring (1 week). Phase 3: Optional opt-in for select Private customers with per-site operator assistance (2-4 weeks). Phase 4: Gradual ramp to 100% with monitoring-based automated promotion. Rollback: flip routing to legacy collector-forward path and revoke enclave routing route entries.
